title: Declining balance depreciation

match.reason: No existing point teaches declining balance depreciation; compound interest and exponential decay are related ideas but not the same formula or context.

draft.title: Declining balance depreciation
card: Depreciation is the fall in an asset's value over time. Declining balance depreciation takes off a fixed percentage of the asset's current value each year.
S = V₀(1 − r)ⁿ. S is the salvage value (the value after n years), V₀ is the starting value, r is the yearly rate as a decimal and n is the number of years.
The percentage is taken from a smaller value each year, so the dollar loss gets smaller each year.
draft.remember: Multiply by (1 − r) once for each year. The value falls, but the rate stays the same.

a.q: A van is worth $40 000 and loses 15% of its value each year. What is its value after 2 years?
a.why: S = 40 000 × 0.85² = 40 000 × 0.7225 = $28 900. The value $28 000 comes from taking 15% of $40 000 off each year, which ignores that the percentage applies to the smaller current value.

b.q: Priya's laptop cost $2000 and depreciates by 20% each year on the declining balance. What is its value after 3 years?
b.why: S = 2000 × 0.8³ = 2000 × 0.512 = $1024. The value $800 comes from taking 20% of the original price off each year, which ignores that each year's loss is taken from the smaller current value.
b.clue: The factor each year is 1 − 0.20, used three times.

check.summary: No problems found. The formula, the worked example and both answers ($28 900 and $1024) are correct, and the explanations correctly identify the 'percentage of the original value' error behind $28 000 and $800.
